points.quote: Anything that holds a resource implements `IDisposable`, which has a `dispose()` method. An event subscription is also an `IDisposable`, so `emitter.event(listener)` returns the handle that unsubscribes it.
`Disposable` is the base class for owners. It has an internal `DisposableStore`, and subclasses call `this._register(x)` so `x` is disposed along with the owner.
`DisposableStore` is a bag of disposables that are all disposed together. ... `toDisposable(fn)` wraps a cleanup callback.
`MutableDisposable` and `MandatoryMutableDisposable` hold a single replaceable resource. Assigning a new value disposes the old one.
`ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite()` in `src/vs/base/test/common/utils.ts` installs a `DisposableTracker` for each test and fails the test if any disposable is still alive afterwards.
